task: False-positive audit: manually check historical price-spike candidates for an identifiable public news or live-event cause

method.dataset: ml/data/spikes.parquet (32,156 Polymarket/Kalshi candidates; 1-minute histories; candidate period 2026-08-04T07:39Z to 2026-10-15T06:03Z)
method.candidate_rule: The ML replay's |delta| >= 0.03 within <= 10 minutes, with a 10-minute cooldown; it is not identical to the live detector's 5-point/volatility triggers.
method.scorer: server/ml/model.json via server/ml/scorer.js predictFeatures applied to the stored point-in-time feature columns; likely cutoff pReal >= 0.593.
method.selection: Deterministic seeded sample (seed 20261015), one row per event group: 12 candidates with pReal >= 0.593 and 12 below. Equal allocation intentionally oversamples below-threshold candidates; population stratum weights are therefore used for the combined plain-rule estimate.
method.news_check: Targeted public web searches for exact market/team wording and the UTC spike date; a positive requires a source describing a specific, plausible event/news catalyst at or near the spike. A match merely occurring that day or the eventual outcome does not count as a confirmed catalyst. No result means 'not found in this search', not proof that nothing happened.
method.precision_definition: Fraction with a publicly identifiable, time-plausible event/news catalyst in this sample. This is stricter and different from the model report's y30 label (move retains >=50% after 30 minutes).

unfiltered_plain_rule.note: 4/24 sample rows had a specific, time-plausible public event/news catalyst. Using the actual 83.3%/16.7% score-stratum mix leaves the point estimate at 16.7% because both equal-sized strata had 2/12 positives.

sample_estimate.interpretation: This tiny, news-search-based sample shows no measurable precision gain from the likely cutoff (16.7% in both strata); it is far too small and noisy to overturn the held-out y30 result in ml/REPORT.md (63.3% real for the plain threshold rule versus 65% among pReal >= 0.593). These figures answer different questions: news discoverability versus future price-move retention.

caveats: The balanced score-stratum sample is small (12 per band), with wide uncertainty. The news-found precision is a manual web-discoverability measure, not a general estimate of all real information events.
A web search that finds no article is not proof the move had no cause; live scores, low-coverage games, private/social channels, and time zone/reporting delays limit identification.
Several sampled candidates are just before a scheduled game, esports match, or market settlement; candidate-price movement alone does not prove the live detector would fire at that exact timestamp.
This replay candidate rule (3 points in 10 minutes, 1-minute grid) differs from live polling/detection (5 points and/or z-score), so the estimates should not be presented as production precision.
The shipped pReal model predicts 30-minute price retention, not whether journalists publish an article or whether the move has an explainable news cause.
